subject.title: ci: accept trusted unsigned release merge heads

question: Should Full Release Validation intentionally trust an unsigned commit when it is the exact canonical release-branch head and exact merge commit of one PR whose unique merger currently has maintain or admin permission?
rationale: This changes the release provenance trust policy; source review supports the narrow rule, but accepting that boundary requires explicit owner intent rather than automation inference.

options.title: Approve Narrow Rule
options.body: Accept the exact-merge rule after exact-head checks and focused acceptance/rejection proof confirm the boundary behaves as intended.

options.title: Require Executable Matrix
options.body: Hold landing until the workflow provenance logic is exercised against representative GitHub payloads rather than source-pattern assertions alone.

options.title: Keep Signed-Only Policy
options.body: Do not accept unsigned release heads and instead require release branches to produce a verifiable signed commit before validation.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Rule
recommendation.body: Accept the exact-merge rule after exact-head checks and focused acceptance/rejection proof confirm the boundary behaves as intended.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the workflow and is the strongest history-backed owner of this newly established release provenance policy.
